patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — BigCommerce and Medusa share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose BigCommerce only if your buying job matches “Open-SaaS ecommerce platform — Core $39/mo ($29 annual), Growth $105 ($79), Scale $399 ($2” rather than Medusa's shape. Choose Medusa only if your buying job matches “Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299” rather than BigCommerce's shape. Workflow advantage: BigCommerce leans catalog-management, wholesale-b2b; Medusa leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — BigCommerce and Medusa share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: BigCommerce is Open-SaaS ecommerce platform — Core $39/mo ($29 annual), Growth $105 ($79), Scale $399 ($299); GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees; Medusa is Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299, Enterprise custom. No GMV tax..
- Workflow coverage skew: BigCommerce-leaning catalog-management, wholesale-b2b vs Medusa-leaning —.
- Researched limits: BigCommerce — 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription; Medusa — Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX.

Limitations — BigCommerce: 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription; Native POS/retail depth trails Shopify/Square for omnichannel-first merchants; Medusa: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX; Not a WordPress-native plugin path (see WooCommerce).

Poor-fit cases: BigCommerce is a poor fit when that limitation bites: 2026 GMV thresholds and open payment provider fees complicate TCO versus headline subscription · Medusa is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX · Avoid BigCommerce if you actually need Medusa's motion (Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
